newsitem.title: USA: U.S. new home sales slightly lower in September.
newsitem.headline: U.S. new home sales slightly lower in September.

text.p: Sales of new homes edged lower in September from August's torrid pace as the housing market remained buoyant, according to Commerce Department figures released on Wednesday.

The department said sales of new homes slipped 0.5 percent in September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 816,000. That was just below August's revised rate of 820,000, but was still the second-highest level since April 1986.
The department had originally estimated the August sales pace at 832,000. Wall Street analysts had expected sales to drop to a 768,000 annual rate in September.
Much of the strength in the housing market last month occured in the Northeast, where sales increased a whopping 41.4 percent, to their highest level since April 1993.
Sales in the Midwest, which had risen sharply in August, fell back in September, dropping by 15.6 percent.
National sales have exceeded a 700,000 annualized pace for nine straight months. The last time that happened was between 1976 and 1979, when sales topped that level for 36 months.
The National Association of Realtors said last week that sales of existing, or used, homes fell by 2.9 percent in September, the fourth straight monthly decline.
The association blamed higher mortgage rates for the drop in sales but still described the underlying state of the housing market as relatively strong.

The average rate for a 30-year mortgage rose to 8.23 percent in September from 8.0 percent in August, according to the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. But rates have since dropped back down to an average 7.92 percent in October.
